page: Amazon Web Services m8gn.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and ARMv9 architecture. It features 16 dedicated physical cores (16 vCPUs at one thread per core) powered by the AWS Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, supported by 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. No discrete GPU accelerators or local NVMe storage drives are bundled, relying on networked Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent storage alongside a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations highlight substantial memory throughput and multi-threaded processing capabilities. The platform achieves a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3343.73, backed by uncached memory read bandwidth of 296.75 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 138.43 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is robust, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 16006.0 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaching 203.79 GB/sec. Database operations in PassMark place in the top quartile at 24267.2 ops, complemented by 34.54 million Redis SET operations per second. Conversely, single-threaded metrics, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1895.0 and stress-ng single-core score of 1707.09, remain in the middle tier. CPU-based large language model inference shows diminished throughput, particularly in token generation.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, the dedicated single-threaded ARM cores provide predictable compute density without hyperthreading resource contention. The integration of 50 Gbps baseline networking enables high throughput for distributed services. The instance is well matched for mid-tier relational and in-memory database engines, containerized microservices, high-bandwidth data ingestion, CI/CD compilation tasks, and general-purpose enterprise application serving where consistent multi-core throughput and high memory bandwidth are prioritized over local disk caching.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gn.4xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by 16 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores operating at 2.8 GHz under the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The configuration provides 64.0 GB of system memory, delivering a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU, paired with a 50 Gbps baseline network interface. It features no local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on remote EBS volumes. Benchmark testing demonstrates exceptional memory subsystem throughput, recording a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3343.73 alongside strong uncached read bandwidth of 296.75 GB/sec. Multi-core compute performance is solid, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 16006.0 and competitive database operational rates. With predictable dedicated core execution and high network capacity, the m8gn.4xlarge is suited for scalable web services, microservices backends, continuous integration pipelines, and distributed in-memory or networked database workloads.
